ELITE.asof: Verified online Sep 21, 2026 via web search (iaclarington.com, newswire.ca and iaconnected.ia.ca full pages remained largely unfetchable directly; sourcing today came from Wealth Professional, the Globe and Mail's syndication of a Newswire.ca release, and several TSX-launch trade outlets, which materially improved on last run's advisor-portal-only sourcing). The single biggest development this run is a much better-sourced version of the portfolio-manager-handover story flagged as 'twice-corroborated but not primary-confirmed' on Sep 19/26: Wealth Professional (via a Newswire.ca release also carried by the Globe and Mail) reports that Sébastien Mc Mahon has stepped back as portfolio manager on 33 funds following his appointment as Chief Economist of iA Financial Group, with iAGAM's Asset Allocation team — led by Tej Rai (managing director, asset allocation) and Alex Bellefleur (SVP, head of research) — taking over. The 33 affected funds span fixed income, Canadian and global equity, balanced and SRI mandates across the Elite, IA Clarington, IA Wealth and Inhance product lines; investment objectives, risk ratings and strategies are stated as unchanged. This is a materially stronger, primary-adjacent source than the advisor-portal page this feed had been citing, and it also explains that page's narrower claim (a Sep 14/26 handover of four segregated — i.e., insurance-wrapped — funds to the same Rai/Bellefleur team): the segregated-fund page is almost certainly describing the insurance-wrapped counterpart of this same broader mutual-fund reassignment, not a separate event. A second, unrelated PM change was also confirmed in the same release: Amit Shah takes over as lead portfolio manager on the IA Clarington QV Canadian Small Cap Fund and Class following Steven Kim's departure, after five years working alongside Kim on the strategy — this fund is not one of the four core mandates tracked in this feed but is noted here under 'PM changes.' Separately, the previously-ambiguous new Active ETF ticker is now resolved: iA Clarington's new International Multifactor Equity Fund (underlying mutual fund launched Jul 27/26, run by iAGAM using a 30+ factor quality/momentum/value framework) trades under ETF ticker IIME (not IMFE) on the TSX, confirmed via CNBC, Kalkine, TradingView and Stockhouse; the market-open ceremony was Sep 18/26, and the Series ETF management fee is 0.50%. On tariffs, today's research resolves the ambiguity flagged on Sep 19/26 about whether a 'Sep 29/26 import ban' was a duplicate or a further step: it is a further, distinct escalation. The timeline is now: a US 50% tariff on $27.6B of Canadian goods took effect Aug 22/26; Canada's retaliatory 15/25/50% counter-tariffs on 700+ US product categories (including doubling steel/aluminum duties to 50%) took effect Sep 8/26, alongside a $5.42B CAD federal support package; and, separately, the US is set to ban imports of Canadian dairy products, motorcycles and alcoholic beverages starting Sep 29/26 (8 days away) via a further presidential action — with President Trump also threatening to block Bombardier aircraft sales in the US unless it manufactures domestically. On sub-advisors: no fresh September-dated PIMCO or Loomis Sayles commentary was found today beyond what's already on file (PIMCO's Monthly Income Fund (Canada) ≈30% of the Elite Core Plus Global Fixed Income Pool; Loomis Sayles Alpha Engine Perspectives pieces dated Sep 1, Aug 25 and Jul 28/26). iA Clarington's overall AUM (>$26B, Jul 31/26) and iAGAM's firm-wide AUM ($156B, Jun 30/26) are both carried forward unchanged. The four Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios Advisor Lunch & Learn events (Sep 22 Ajax/Markham, Sep 23 London, Sep 24 Kitchener, Sep 25 Oakville) are now 1-4 days away.
